a: ‘By the fig and the olive’: Allah swore by the fig and the olive, or He swore by the blessed land that grows them; ‘at-tin’ is the name of the well-known fruit.
The olive: a fruit-bearing oil tree; its fruit is eaten after salting, and oil is pressed from it.
‘Mount Sinin’: Mount Sinai — the mountain of intimate converse for the one spoken to, Musa, peace be upon him; it is a mountain near Aylah.
‘Mount Sinin’: Mount Sinai — the mountain of intimate converse for the one spoken to, Musa, peace be upon him; it is a mountain near Aylah.
‘Hadha’: a demonstrative for the near masculine singular; the ‘ha’ is for drawing attention.
‘The secure city’: the one in which whoever enters is protected; safe, with no fear in it; what is meant is Makkah.
‘Laqad’: the ‘lam’ is the response to the oath; ‘qad’ is a particle conveying certainty (realisation).
We brought into being without a prior model; and Allah’s creation is from nothingness.
The male and the female of the children of Adam.
A preposition conveying the meaning of state.
‘The best stature’: the most perfect proportion and the best form.
A particle of resumption conveying sharing in the ruling and sequence, usually with an interval.
We made his outcome and his end.
‘The lowest of the low’: the least degree of the low; what is meant is that his return is to the Fire if he disbelieves.

A particle of exception; the exception here is connected (the excepted belongs to the named group).
A relative noun for a group of males.
They acknowledged the oneness of Allah and the truthfulness of His messengers, and submitted to Allah with obedience and to the Messenger with following.
A recompense for the deed and a compensation for it.
It occurs sometimes in the meaning of ‘illa’ (except), sometimes in the meaning of ‘duna’ (without), and sometimes as an adjective.
‘Ma’: a noun used to ask about what is not rational, and about the reality of a thing or its quality.
‘So what makes you deny the Recompense after this’: what drives you to deny the recompense after the resurrection and reckoning.
A vague adverb whose meaning is understood by annexation to what follows it; it is the opposite of ‘before’.
‘Ad-din’: the recompense after the resurrection and reckoning.
‘Alaysa’: for affirmation, that is, to establish the attribution of its predicate to its subject.

A name of the Most High Essence, unique in divinity, whose existence is necessary, worshipped by right; it is the Word of Majesty (lafz al-jalalah) comprehending the meanings of all of Allah’s perfect attributes.
‘The wisest of judges’: the most knowledgeable of them and the most just in judgement.
